sector_model: nonfinancial: specialty pharma with product launch; revenue concentration, margin trajectory, cash and securities, litigation and regulatory events; TTM FCF understates the new run rate
thesis: Corcept (cortisol modulation pharma) closed 72.77 on 2026-11-06 (down from 81.93 on 11-03; -9.6% on 11-05 after Q3 results). Market cap about 7.96B on 109,443,109 shares (10-Q cover, 2026-10-22). Q3 revenue 340.5M (+64%) with the ovarian-cancer product Lifyorli at 91.4M in its second quarter and Korlym plus authorized generic 249.1M; Q3 operating income 114.7M versus 10.2M a year earlier. TTM net income about 162M gives about 49x, TTM FCF about 195M (2.4% yield), but Q3 operating income annualized is about 459M, about 16x on enterprise value of about 7.3B (market cap less 662M cash and securities, no debt identified). The market seems to price a transient launch peak and a regulatory binary (relacorilant hypercortisolism PDUFA 2026-12-17); the opposing evidence is the sharp operating leverage and a net cash balance.
counterthesis: The Q3 profit is a single quarter; 9M operating income is only 106.4M, so the TTM multiple is high and the forward case depends on Lifyorli sustaining about 90M+ a quarter. Korlym faces generic competition (Teva litigation status not read) and Medicare pricing pressure under the IRA. A class action covers October 2024 to December 2025 after the December 2025 complete response letter. SG&A rose 47% in 9M (466.7M vs 318.5M) and is guided higher; stock-based compensation was 81.9M in 9M (about 11% of revenue); buybacks have nearly stopped (5.7M). Income tax benefit of 16.5M in 9M and a negative tax line inflate net income relative to operating income. A second CRL for relacorilant would remove the main pipeline value.
invalidation: Lifyorli sequential revenue declining; Korlym hypercortisolism revenue falling faster than 10% a year from generics; second complete response letter on 2026-12-17; SG&A growth outpacing revenue growth for two quarters; adverse securities litigation outcome; operating margin falling below 20%.
